target.consumer: universal worker recovery executor and 50-worker stress verifier

title: Make recovery claims atomic under contention
problem: The current stale/recovery library evaluates active_overlap before persistence, then buildRecoveryAttempt assigns a unique append-only recovery-claim path. Under high parallelism that is a TOCTOU gap: several workers can all observe no overlapping recovery and each successfully create a different recovery-claim file for the same opportunity. Live evidence on 2026-09-17 showed at least four new kernel recovery claims between 09:51 and 09:54 and at least five new page-thread recovery claims between 09:51 and 09:55, while neither opportunity yet had a durable RETURN at the preflight checks. Append-only lineage is preserved, but exclusive recovery ownership is not established by the current mechanism.
mission: Implement and canary deterministic per-opportunity recovery arbitration so concurrent stale recoverers produce exactly one recovery owner and durable loser evidence before any recovery run or target mutation, while retaining CAS-safe stale takeover, late-return reconciliation and append-only lineage.
acceptance: A concurrent N-worker recovery race for one opportunity yields exactly one recovery lease/owner before any recovery run enters substantive work.
Recovery losers persist durable LOST_EXISTING or equivalent receipts and do not create competing recovery runs or write target scope.
The arbitration key is deterministic per opportunity rather than a unique recovery-attempt filename, so create-if-absent or equivalent host atomicity decides the first owner.
If the winning recovery itself becomes stale, takeover requires a generation/lease CAS transition with re-fetched owner identity; stale overwrite is impossible.
A durable original RETURN suppresses or reconciles recovery without deleting either lineage, and recency alone never grants authority.
A live contention canary reproduces the current multi-recovery race before the fix and demonstrates one-owner behavior after the fix with machine-auditable receipts.

goal_relevance.reason: The universal swarm canary requires safe stale recovery and collision behavior under high parallelism; the observed duplicate recovery ownership directly attacks that gate.

unblock_value.reason: Kernel and Page Thread are gate-unlocking opportunities, so duplicate recoverers on them create the highest-risk overlapping-write condition exactly where recovery is meant to reduce stalls.

information_gain.reason: The live broad wave produced empirical contention that static stale-threshold tests did not falsify; an atomic recovery race canary converts it into measurable winner/loser evidence.

regression_prevention.reason: A deterministic recovery lock plus multi-worker race test would prevent read-before-write active_overlap checks from silently regressing into duplicate recoveries.

falsification: Two concurrent eligible recoverers can both acquire ownership for the same opportunity generation.
A losing recoverer can create a substantive recovery run or touch the target write scope.
An expired recovery owner can be replaced without checking the exact prior lease generation/identity.
A late original RETURN can be overwritten, discarded, or auto-demoted solely because recovery acquired a lease.
The live canary cannot reconcile winner/loser receipts with actual recovery ownership.
dedup_note: The completed O-SWARM-LEASE-RETRY-BUILD-V1 supplies stale thresholds, active-overlap evaluation, CAS decisions and append-only recovery candidates, but its own known limit leaves persistence to a separate executor; buildRecoveryAttempt writes a unique recovery-attempt path and therefore does not provide an atomic same-opportunity mutex. P-04df793d0713-e1aaac9c proposes durable live claim-attempt receipts for ordinary create-if-absent claim flow; this proposal is narrower and distinct because it requires exclusive recovery ownership plus stale lease takeover semantics.
